answer: Deposit-decay identity pricing makes each new identity post a refundable deposit that decays over time toward a nadir reached only after sustained honest activity, so creating many identities at once locks capital that loses value the faster it is abandoned. An agent's reputation score acts as the anchor for its withdrawal rights, meaning mass-registered accounts cannot cash out until they build independent history. The system reads the whole account graph as a nebula of linked registrations, and clusters of new identities sharing funding sources face proportionally higher deposits.
